case_title: A.M. Mohan v. The State Represented by SHO and Another
high_court_outcome: High Court rejected the petition to quash FIR
neutral_facts: The prosecution case is that in 2016, accused No. 2 approached the complainant for help to clear a loan. Accused No. 2 claimed to have business with accused No. 1, who runs a hotel and real estate business. The complainant agreed to provide financial assistance to accused No. 1 for business projects, with repayment terms. The complainant transferred a total of Rs. 1,60,01,000/- to accused Nos. 1 and 2. Accused No. 1 executed a registered mortgage deed in favor of the complainant. The complainant also entered into an unregistered memorandum of understanding and transferred additional funds to accused No. 1. Accused No. 1 executed a registered deed of General Power of Attorney in favor of the complainant for land purchased from accused No. 3. The complainant transferred Rs. 20,00,000/- to accused No. 3's bank account. Accused No. 1 sold the land to third parties and failed to return the mortgaged amount. The complainant alleges that accused Nos. 1 and 2 cheated him out of Rs. 16,01,00,000/- through fraudulent means. A FIR was registered against accused Nos. 1, 2, and 3 for offences punishable under IPC s. 420 r/w s. 34. The High Court rejected the appellant's petition to quash the FIR, directing the investigation to continue. The Supreme Court quashed the FIR and charge-sheet against the appellant, finding no dishonest inducement or fraud on his part.
